about.title: Ukiah Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Falls happen in ordinary places around Ukiah — a grocery store on N State Street, a restaurant near Talmage Road, a business lot off Airport Park Boulevard. What turns a fall into a legitimate claim is proof that the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and didn't fix it or warn you. That's why the first hours and days matter so much: photos of the spill, torn carpet, or broken step; witness names; and a written incident report all help establish what the owner knew. Surveillance footage is often the strongest evidence, but many businesses only retain it for a short window before it's erased. Ukiah's population is modest, and many falls happen at local shops, apartment complexes, or public buildings rather than large chains, which makes prompt documentation even more important. LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney who understands how to investigate these claims and preserve evidence before it disappears.

whyChoose.title: Why Notice and Timing Matter in These Claims

items.title: Proving the Owner Knew or Should Have Known
items.desc: California law requires showing the property owner had actual or constructive notice of the hazard before your fall. An attorney can help gather maintenance logs, complaint history, and witness statements that speak to this notice requirement.

items.title: Preserving Surveillance Video Before It's Gone
items.desc: Many Ukiah businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of that video can make the difference in showing exactly how the hazard formed and how long it existed.

items.title: Understanding Comparative Fault Rules
items.desc: California applies pure comparative fault, meaning any partial responsibility you might share doesn't automatically bar your claim — it can simply reduce the recovery in proportion to fault. An attorney can help present the facts fairly in that framework.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Ukiah?
items.answer: Generally you have two years from the date of the fall to file a claim under California law. If a government-owned property — like a city building near S State Street — was involved, the deadline is much shorter and requires an earlier claim process. Speaking with an attorney soon after the fall helps make sure no deadline is missed.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for my own fall?
items.answer: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still pursue a claim even if you bear some responsibility for the fall. Any compensation would be adjusted to reflect your share of fault, but it wouldn't necessarily eliminate your claim. An independent attorney can help evaluate how fault might be allocated in your situation.

items.question: Does it matter that Ukiah is a smaller city with fewer big-box stores?
items.answer: It can. Many falls in Ukiah happen at locally owned shops, apartment buildings, or public facilities rather than large corporate chains, which sometimes means less formal incident-reporting systems and shorter video retention. That makes it even more important to document the scene yourself and get evidence requests out quickly.
